message.content:
Both \(B\) and \(P\) lie on line \(m\), so \(\overrightarrow{BP}\) is parallel to the direction vector of \(m\):

\[
\overrightarrow{BP} \parallel \begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Since \(\overrightarrow{BP}\) is the projection of \(\overrightarrow{BA}\) onto \(\begin{pmatrix}v_1\\v_2\end{pmatrix}\), the vector \(\begin{pmatrix}v_1\\v_2\end{pmatrix}\) must also be parallel to \(\overrightarrow{BP}\). Hence

\[
\begin{pmatrix}v_1\\v_2\end{pmatrix}
= k\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}
= \begin{pmatrix}4k\\3k\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Given \(v_1+v_2=-7\),

\[
4k+3k=-7 \implies 7k=-7 \implies k=-1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\begin{pmatrix}v_1\\v_2\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}-4\\-3\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}-4\\-3\end{pmatrix}}\).
